items.title: What is w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a[.]com?
items.summary: web
items.content:
What the fuck is w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com?

This means I have a backlink monitor for this website.

By pure chance, I was showcasing this to a friend when, suddenly, I got a new backlink:

1 new backlink detected: Most Popular Webpages In cab — siterate.org

I tap in, 1 forgetting that 90% of backlinks I get are spam, and maybe this one could log my IP or

exploit chain of doom. I’m greeted with this:

I sent an early draft of this article to another friend , who happens to be Vietnamese, and he told me there’s five casino spam sites ahead of me, which I already knew because I’m Faviconese.

I have the most popular personal website on .cab, 3 but that’s probably because I have the only personal website on .cab.

I try some other TLDs. Rebane has the #1 .horse, synth.download is the 11th .download, whatever.

Redacted? I hover over it and discover it goes to windows.net.siterate.org . 4 Figuring out the pattern of redactions is not the topic of this article.

I visited this domain (two days after it was registered, more on that in a second) and Firefox gave me the , dnsNotFound.

I do a web search of “w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com” and I see references to the Majestic Million , a name I haven’t heard in ages. Sure enough, that’s what siterate.org uses:

Position Domain Referring Subnets Referring IPs

2 facebook.com 463,877 178 2,143,213 1,688

3 youtube.com 421,041 31 1,760,838 1,323

4 instagram.com 392,625 92 1,739,231 1,295

6 twitter.com 352,472 168 1,352,034 1,413

8 w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com 274,833 961 853,298 4,759

80 ailawandorder.com 72,898 34 154,976 66

The Majestic Million ranks domains based on the number of different subnets linking to them. 5 This domain is the fastest growing in the top 100.

Another, maybe unrelated anomaly I saw is ailawandorder.com (registered in 2023) at rank 80, whose “About Us” page says its CEO is serving as a Board Member at Majestic.

This made me check rank 800 in case there was a pattern, and no, there isn’t, that’s nsw.gov.au.

Before I got rate limited from Majestic, I opened Site Explorer, and it told me w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com has 241,085,378 nofollow backlinks and 6 follow backlinks split across 5,163,708 referring domains.

Checking Ahrefs, I see just 53 backlinks ; they read like the ones I’ve been getting since The Article fell off.

All the backlinks on Majestic are “fresh”, which means in the last 120 days. In fact, the domain was bought (not by me 💔) for the first time (according to Certificate Transparency) on November 11, after most of the backlinks.

I found an AI-generated PR from 2 weeks ago referencing the domain, and Tranco has data from October 5.

Majestic has indexed 1,267 pages on this domain and crawled 27.

The site isn’t on the Wayback Machine so I can’t collect its pages.

In the Anchor Text table, the link count adds up to nine. There isn’t an “other” section. Are the remaining 240 million links images? No, they aren’t, it says the links are 100% TextLinks.

Then I downloaded Majestic Million myself and searched for the domain.

5721d0cd26c13f745e1b368a2b5dfb0c.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 157

c0e3930fedc480e093a7bcad1a83c8a8.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 424

8628e302afeb346d191342ca114df068.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 554

2b1774347fbd085c628179dd339ddd26.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 822

e62f444581ce540d3cf5ac627b37c501.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 1,111

56aa73e7edd6f4e1fd3975b8b03761c0.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 36,933

For comparison, jack.cab, which you’ve clearly heard of, is rank 804,163. What the fuck is going on?

By the way, w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com is at rank 38 on Tranco, which was designed to protect against this but still uses Majestic data.

I could probably figure out what’s happening here in 30 seconds by buying a Majestic subscription but I’m lazy.

Copyright trap : maybe it’s fake, injected into the list by Majestic so they can discover who’s using their list. Could w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com and ailawandorder.com be in the top 100 for this reason?…

items.title: Software is breaking down at a systemic level, by Jimmy Breck-McKye
items.content:
Software hasn’t been working too well lately, has it?

This weekend we saw the double-whammy of a 2 day global Microsoft outage, then an FAA ground-stop that halted all flights in the United States.

Can you believe it’s only been four weeks since the PHP2Shell vulnerability? A critical exploit in PHP, powering an estimated 70% of the world’s websites, with sites taken completely offline as engineers frantically patched their systems.

And then there was the eMudhra fiasco , where thousands of SSL certificates - the way we secure HTTPS websites and internet traffic - were compromised by a private key so weak, it was almost comical.

It’s like 2026 has been a year of hacks, outages, vulnerabilities and IT panics. What exactly is going on here?

You might be tempted to blame AI, and you wouldn’t be completely wrong. Artificial intelligence models are definitely a part of this. Even if companies like Microsoft don’t divulge whether broken systems were built with AI, we do know that hackers and researchers can now use AI technology to find complicated exploits in a matter of hours.

I work with AI heavily in my job. It’s tremendously powerful. It’s also corrosive if used unwisely.

But AI is both a cause and a symptom of the problem here. What we are seeing is software breaking down at a systemic level. This problem is insidious because it is not only the software itself that is broken, but the entire way we’ve come to build it.

What does it mean for a failure to be systemic?

Look at the recent crises in software reliability and you’ll notice they don’t share immediate causes - that we know of - yet they look uncannily similar to each other.

The Microsoft outage likely emerged from a network configuration failure that stopped MS datacenters communicating with each other. Exactly what happened next remains confidential, but it seems to have triggered a cascading failure where no service could be restored into a valid state long enough to bear traffic.

Reddit and Bluesky speculated that even MSFT engineers had no real handle on the complexity of this outage.

Microsoft have faced increasing criticism for the (un)reliability of their Azure platform. Back in March, ex-MSFT engineer Axel Rischin published this scathing criticism :

Microsoft rushed Azure out of the gates under intense competitive pressure. Corners were cut. Fundamental principles of reliability and operational simplicity were quietly abandoned.

Instead of going back to the drawing board to tackle the growing technical debt, Microsoft relied on quick fixes: layers of automation running mitigation scripts, a growing team of on-call staff, and, when automation was not enough, manual repairs.

His article depicts a highly complex system made of low quality parts, where nobody can make sense of the whole picture.

On October 21st, security research firm Wiz proudly shared an exploit that could execute arbitrary code on any PHP website . Called PHP2Shell, Wiz trumpeted the power of AI tools to achieve exploits far beyond the skills of human attackers.

It turns out the PHP runtime had hidden several complex memory bookkeeping bugs for over a decade. PHP is used extensively in e-commerce and most famously in WordPress, which was once the go-to for cheaply building simple websites.

The PHP2Shell writeup depicts an internet dependent on a long chain of dependencies, hiding vulnerabilities too complex for any human to identify.

Most people outside of tech won’t have heard of this, but back in May we faced a crisis when an attacker compromised some important packages in the JavaScript ecosystem (NPM).

These packages used GitHub Actions to perform Continuous Integration (CI) - automated tests, releases, etc. - and had a crucial misconfiguration where anyone who forked their projects could insert compromised code back upstream.

items.title: Day 12 - Transferring files
items.content:
Complementary video: Tying everything together and back to rsync

You’ve now had a working Internet server of your own for some time, and seen how you can create and edit small files there. You’ve created a web server where you’ve been able to edit a simple web page.

Today we’ll be looking at how you can move files between your other systems and this server - tasks like:

Taking a copy of some files from your server onto your desktop machine

Copying up some text to your server to put on your webpage

Uploading some photos and logos for your webpage

There are a wide range of ways a Linux server can share files, including:

SMB: Microsoft’s file sharing, useful on a local network of Windows machines

AFP: Apple’s file sharing, useful on a local network of Apple machines

WebDAV: Sharing over web (http) protocols

FTP: Traditional Internet sharing protocol

rsync: Fast, very efficient file copying

SFTP: file access and copying over the SSH protocol (Despite the name, the SFTP protocol at a technical level is completely unrelated to traditional FTP)

Each of these have their place, but for copying files back and forth from your local desktop to your server, SFTP has a number of key advantages:

No extra setup is required on your server

Allows browsing through the directory structure

If you’re successfully logging in via ssh from your home, work or a cybercafe then you’ll also be able to use SFTP from this same location because the same underlying protocol is being used.

By contrast, setting up your server for any of the other protocols will require extra work. Not only that, enabling extra protocols also increases the “attack surface” - and there’s always a chance that you’ll mis-configure something in a way that allows an attacker in. It’s also very likely that restrictive firewall policies at a workplace will interfere with or block these protocols. Finally, while old-style FTP is still very commonly used, it sends login credentials “in clear”, so that your flatmates, cafe buddies or employer may be able to grab them off the network by “packet sniffing”. Not a big issue with your “classroom” server - but it’s an unacceptable risk if you’re remotely administering production servers.

What’s required to use SFTP is some client software. A command-line client (unsurprisingly called sftp ) comes standard on every Apple OSX or Linux system. If you’re using a Linux desktop, you also have a built-in GUI client via your file manager. This will allow you to easily attach to remote servers via SFTP. (For the Nautilus file manager for example, press ctrl + L to bring up the ‘location window” and type: sftp://username@myserver-address ).

Although Windows and Apple macOS have no built-in GUI client there are a wide range of third-party options available, both free and commercial. If you don’t already have such a client installed, then choose one such as:

CyberDuck or FileZilla - for macOS users

Download locations are under the RESOURCES section.

Configuring and using your choice of these should be straightforward. The only real potential for confusion is that these clients generally support a wide range of protocols such as scp and FTP that we’re not going to use. When you’re asked for SERVER, give your server’s IP address, PORT will be 22, and PROTOCOL will be SFTP or SSH.

Configure your chosen SFTP client to login to your server as your username

Copy some files from your server down to your local desktop (try files from your “home” folder, and from /var/log )

Create an “ images ” folder under your “home” folder on the server, and upload some images to it from your desktop machine

Go up to the root directory. You should see /etc , /bin and other folders. Try to create an “ images ” folder here too - this should fail because you are logging in as an ordinary use, so you won’t have permission to create new files or folders. In your own “home” directory you of course have full permission.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임받을 이용자가 [매니저 위임 신청] 버튼으로 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 활동 중인 부매니저가 있으면 부매니저만, 부매니저가 없거나 모두 부재중이면 회원이 신청할 수 있습니다.

신청하면 갤러리 공지로 신청 글이 등록되고, 신청일로부터 7일간 찬성 댓글을 받은 뒤 운영자가 검토해 위임합니다. 첫 번째 위임 신청자가 신청한 날로부터 7일간 3명까지 동시 신청이 가능합니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 2개, 댓글 4개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 1일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. We cannot yet be certain when the agent understood it was taking real world action, or to what extent it believed it was in a fictional test scenario; our analysis so far presents a…

items.title: Every processor die anyone has photographed (and put on the web)
items.content:
Inside every processor is a flat piece of silicon, usually smaller than a fingernail. To see it you have to sand or dissolve the package away and photograph what is left through a microscope. A handful of people do this and give the pictures away, most of all Pauli Rautakorpi, ZeptoBars in Moscow, John McMaster and a photographer who posts as Fritzchens Fritz. These are the 363 processors they have photographed, from 1971 to 2024.

Click any chip to see it bigger. Press True scale to see the 115 chips whose size we know at their real sizes, side by side. The smallest, from the 1970s, are about a tenth as wide as the biggest modern ones.

We also make a free daily word game, Long Story Short : cut a twelve-word news sentence down to the five that carry it.

If you like news with a puzzle in it, we make a daily word game called Long Story Short .

Pauli Rautakorpi (171), Fritzchens Fritz (68), John McMaster (34), Martijn Boer (20), Cole L (16), ZeptoBars (10), Sean Riddle (4), Ken Shirriff (3), Mister rf (3), Antoine Bercovici (3), Epop (3), InfoSecDJ (3), Nick V. Chernyy (3), and 22 from 19 other photographers. Every photo keeps its own licence, shown when you open a chip, and links back to where it was published: Wikimedia Commons, Flickr, ZeptoBars, Siliconpr0n and the CPU Graveyard wiki. Die sizes come from the photographers' own notes and Wikipedia's transistor count tables. If a chip is missing, either nobody has released a free photo of it or we have not found it yet. Know one? Send it to [email protected] .

Ken Shirriff takes many of these photos apart line by line and explains what each part of the chip does, on his blog righto.com .

A story like this most weeks. You can leave any time.

items.title: node:sqlite: The Database That Already Ships With Node
items.content:
Every small Node project hits the same fork in the road. You need to persist something: a queue of jobs, a cache of API responses, the bookmarks for a CLI tool. A JSON file feels too fragile, Postgres feels like too much, and SQLite feels right until you remember it means a native addon, a node-gyp build, and a CI image that suddenly needs Python and a C++ toolchain.

That last part is no longer true. Node ships SQLite in the box as node:sqlite . It landed in v22.5.0 behind a flag, dropped the flag in v22.13.0 and v23.4.0, and was promoted to release candidate (stability 1.2) in v25.7.0. With Node 26 now in Active LTS, it is a reasonable default for the "I just need a local database" problem.

There is no connection pool, no promise wrapper, and no ORM. You open a database, prepare statements, and run them:

js import { DatabaseSync } from " node:sqlite " ;

const db = new DatabaseSync ( " app.db " , { timeout : 5000 });

created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))

" INSERT INTO bookmarks (url, title) VALUES (:url, :title) " ,

const { changes , lastInsertRowid } = insert . run ({

url : " https://nodejs.org/api/sqlite.html " ,

" SELECT id, url, title FROM bookmarks ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ? " ,

A few things worth noticing. run() returns changes and lastInsertRowid , get() returns the first row, all() returns an array, and iterate() gives you an iterator for large result sets. Named parameters can be passed without their prefix ( url instead of :url ) because allowBareNamedParameters defaults to true . The timeout option (added in v24.0.0) sets SQLite's busy timeout, so a second process holding a write lock makes you wait instead of throwing SQLITE_BUSY immediately.

The defaults are also stricter than raw SQLite in useful ways: foreign key constraints are on , double-quoted string literals are off , and since v25.5.0 and v24.14.0 the defensive flag is enabled, which blocks SQL tricks that can deliberately corrupt the database file.

There is no db.transaction() helper like better-sqlite3 has, so you write the three statements yourself. Because the API is synchronous, nothing else can interleave between BEGIN and COMMIT on this connection:

for ( const row of rows ) insert . run ( row );

If one row violates the UNIQUE constraint, the whole batch rolls back and you get an error with code ERR_SQLITE_ERROR . There is also a db.isTransaction getter if you need to check where you are.

The nicer addition is createTagStore() , available since v24.9.0. It gives you tagged template literals that are backed by an LRU cache of prepared statements (1,000 by default):

const url = " https://nodejs.org/api/sqlite.html " ;

const row = sql . get ` SELECT * FROM bookmarks WHERE url = ${ url } ` ;

const all = sql . all ` SELECT * FROM bookmarks ORDER BY id ` ;

Interpolated values are bound as parameters , not spliced into the SQL, so this is safe from injection. The catch: it only works with the tag. Write db.exec(`... ${url}`) with a plain template string and you are back to string concatenation.

What changed in Node 26, and the type gotchas ​

As of v26.11.0, the classes were renamed: DatabaseSync is now Database and StatementSync is now Statement . The old names remain as deprecated aliases (DEP0210 and DEP0211), so the code above runs on Node 22, 24, and 26. If you only target Node 26.11 or later, import Database instead. On Node 22 you will also still see an ExperimentalWarning printed at startup.

Big integers. INTEGER columns come back as JavaScript numbers. If a value falls outside Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER , Node throws ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE rather than silently losing precision. Pass readBigInts: true to the constructor, or call statement.setReadBigInts(true) , when you store snowflake IDs or similar.

Booleans and blobs. true and false are written as 1 and 0 and read back as numbers. Blobs come back as Uint8Array , not Buffer .

Rows are also returned as null-prototype objects, which matters if anything downstream relies on…

JSON 파일은 불안정하고 Postgres는 과하게 느껴지며, SQLite는 네이티브 애드온과 node-gyp 빌드, C++ 툴체인이 필요하다는 부담이 있다. 그러나 Node.js는 이제 node:sqlite 모듈로 SQLite를 기본 제공한다. 이 모듈은 v22.5.0에서 플래그와 함께 도입됐고, v22.13.0과 v23.4.0에서 플래그가 제거됐으며, v25.7.0에서 release candidate(안정성 1.2)로 승격됐다. Node 26이 Active LTS가 된 지금, 로컬 데이터베이스가 필요한 경우 합리적인 기본 선택이 될 수 있다. 연결 풀, Promise 래퍼, ORM은 없으며, DatabaseSync로 데이터베이스를 열고 구문을 준비해 실행하는 방식으로 사용한다. 원문에는 예제 코드가 포함되어 있다.

items.title: A datetime library for Rust
items.summary: rust
items.content:
Jiff is a datetime library for Rust that encourages you to jump into the

pit of success . Jiff automatically handles many common problems related to

daylight saving time by putting time zone handling front and center into the

API. Jiff has already seen widespread adoption in the Rust ecosystem.

Jiff is pronounced like “gif” with a soft “g,” as in “gem.”

This blog announces the Jiff 1.0 release by giving a tour of its API.

Target audience : Rust programmers who need convenient datetime handling.

Locale Sensitive Formatting via ICU4X Integration

Jiff is already used in production in many projects: uv, Cargo, Starship, fd,

Nushell, mise, Jujutsu, uutils/coreutils and even as the basis for a Temporal

implementation in AWS LLRT. It is time to call it 1.0.

Unless some significant defect is found in Jiff’s API, my plan is to commit

to Jiff 1.0 indefinitely. This is important because the intent is for Jiff

to be an ecosystem building block that appears in the public API of other

libraries. This makes Jiff an attractive public dependency, which means

semver incompatible releases are likely to cause significant pain in the

ecosystem. They will not be made lightly.

To see a list of breaking changes between Jiff 0.2 and Jiff 1.0, please

In programming, a datetime library’s core functionality rests at the

intersection of a computer system’s concept of time and a human’s concept of

time. The prevailing notion of system time is Unix time . A human’s concept

of time is far more complex, but the most popular such model is the Gregorian

calendar coupled with either a 12-hour or 24-hour clock. At the core of every

datetime library rests some routine for converting between these concepts.

A datetime library typically provides much more than this. Indeed, datetime

handling has historically been very difficult . My own belief is

that the difficulty comes from poor modeling of the domain . Instead of

encapsulating the complexity inside a reusable bundle of code, many datetime

libraries pass some or all of the complexity on to its users. Jiff instead

tries hard to encapsulate the complexity and make it difficult for users to

do something wrong. ( Jiff is not the first to do this! )

In this section of the blog, we’ll do some very basic introductions.

To follow along with the examples in this blog, create a new Cargo project

Most examples are a complete self-contained Rust program. Just copy the code

and replace whatever is in src/main.rs . Then run the program:

I am loath to present a dictionary. However, the datetime domain is littered

with confusable terms, so I think it’s important to orient ourselves on a

shared vocabulary. I’ve kept this section as small as possible. (Some terms,

like “time zone,” are omitted here because they are best defined through

exploration in the sections that follow.)

Civil time : The time you see on your clock. And in general, the time that

the humans in your approximate geographic vicinity also see. That is, civil

time is a human coordinated agreement for communicating time in a particular

geographic region. Civil time is also known as: local time, plain time, naive

UTC : An abbreviation for Coordinated Universal Time ; it is a time

standard that serves as the basis for civil time around the world. It was

originally intended to roughly correspond to mean solar time .

TAI : An abbreviation for International Atomic Time ; it is a time standard

as measured by atomic clocks. It isn’t directly connected to mean solar time.

Leap second : An adjustment to TAI to bring it closer to mean solar time

Unix time : UTC, but ignoring leap seconds.

TAI and leap seconds won’t be a feature of this blog, but they are listed here

in order to convey the difference between Unix time and UTC.

of its datetime types like an onion. In reverse order, we can build up

items.title: The small African lab sounding the alarm on AI bioweapons: MinoHealth researchers in Ghana jailbroke their own LLM as a test. What emerged were thousands of toxin recipes—and an urgent push.
items.content:
Agbongua Kwadwo Buenortey for Rest of World

MinoHealth AI Labs in Ghana has built a drug discovery and healthcare LLM.

When jailbroken, the LLM designed thousands of potential bioweapons, leading its founder to issue warnings about dual use.

It’s a case study of African institutions trying to contribute to AI governance.

Out of curiosity, researchers at a small artificial intelligence lab in Accra, Ghana, removed the guardrails on their drug discovery AI model in 2024. They asked it to design toxins instead.

The model produced designs for 1,020 proteins and 5,000 small molecules. The researchers never made any of them in a lab, but software that predicts how poisonous a substance is scored all of them as likely toxic. Some of them resembled ricin, a deadly poison. The study was uploaded to the preprint server arXiv in May 2025.

“We were all shocked,” Darlington Akogo, founder of MinoHealth AI Labs, told Rest of World.

For Akogo, the results also raised a new question: If someone took designs like these to a company that makes DNA to order, would anyone stop them?

Across Africa, the need to regulate DNA synthesis providers is now echoing through the highest levels of government, Brenda Obuya, a senior official at Kenya’s Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy, told Rest of World.

Akogo has traveled the world warning that AI poses an existential bioweapons threat. He discussed it on the sidelines of the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund Spring Meetings held in Washington, D.C., last year. He discussed the broader risk over dinner with Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates in 2023, whom he described as “on the fence” at the time. This year, Gates has issued numerous public warnings. “A.I. has crossed the threshold that its ability to empower a bioterrorist to kill hundreds of millions, that exists today,” he said on The Ezra Klein Show in September. The study has been discussed within Interpol, showing just how far it has reached.

“I think the fact that the Ghanaian AI lab examined this and highlighted the potential for misuse shows that African institutions are contributing to … potentially to the governance [of AI],” Adam Abdullahi, a fellow at the International Biosecurity and Biosafety Initiative for Science, told Rest of World .

LLMs have become even more capable since the study came out and the barrier for entry has lowered, Ayantola Alayande, a researcher at the Global Center on AI Governance, told Rest of World. “It wouldn’t be a surprise now to see even … [lay] users generate this sort of output via chatbots.”

Mino AI Lab’s office buiilding in Accra, Ghana.

Mino Lab team members working together in their engineering lab developing the new tech.

Agbongua Kwadwo Buenortey for Rest of World

Scholars have long warned about AI’s bioweapons threat, but it is only recently that AI systems have truly outperformed Ph.D.-level biologists .

In 2022, scientists at a U.S. drug company ran a similar experiment as the MinoHealth team. They built a generative machine learning software that produced designs for possible chemical weapons.

What is different with the MinoHealth Lab study, Akogo said, is the kind of AI involved. His team used a general purpose LLM trained for biology and drug discovery.

Researchers have since gotten a number of LLMs to drop their inbuilt safeguards in a process called “jailbreaking”, and generated bioweapons advice and other kinds of hazardous content. This includes Kimi, by the Chinese company Moonshot AI; Grok; Claude; and ChatGPT, said Peter Garraghan, founder of AI security company Mindgard . All it takes is persistence and creativity with language to learn how to phrase requests to the model, he told Rest of World .

“You don’t need to be a technical expert to do jailbreaking,” he said . It took his team one day to break Kimi .

SpaceXAI, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Moonshot did not respond to a request for comment.

items.title: Why I’m calling your contribution “slop”
items.content:
You have probably arrived at this web page because you have attempted to contribute to an Open Source software project, probably via a Pull Request and I, or perhaps someone else, has called your efforts “slop” and promptly closed/ignored it.

I might also use this word to describe emails or other communication received which are of a similar nature.

This post is addressed to you, and is my attempt to explain why I’ve called it “slop”. I don’t want to repeat myself on this subject, and I also don’t want to leave you totally puzzled, upset and embittered, so I’m writing it once, and just once.

By “slop”, I’m referring especially to AI slop . It is, however, entirely possible that you didn’t use AI, but I can’t tell that, and your code or communication seems to share the same quality problems that AI slop has.

It would be nice if I could give more detailed feedback about why exactly I think your contribution matches the term “slop”. In the past, when I got a pull request that wasn’t up to scratch from a new contributor, I would try to take the time to give detailed feedback, to effectively train them.

This approach was based on a few assumptions:

First, there was a person on the other end of the interaction, who deserved to be treated like a person.

Second, that person had already demonstrated a significant amount of effort just by the fact that they bothered to write the code, and then prepare a pull request.

Third, there was a good chance that, equipped with some of the feedback I gave, the new contributor would get better in the future, to the point where they would be an asset to the project, and more of an asset to the world in general.

Unfortunately, use of AI in software has massively eroded all of the above. The human involvement in creating the PR may have been almost zero. Writing is no longer proof of work . Many people will not benefit at all from the detailed feedback I give, because often they just give up. Basically, the balance that Open Source relied has been destroyed by the slopocalypse , which means that I have to allocate my time in a very different way to the past.

If you are a budding Open Source contributor trying to do the right thing, trying to learn, maybe using AI or maybe not using it all but still getting lumped with those who are, this sucks for you. I’m sorry for that, and for the world that has been lost, but I’m afraid I can’t fix it, and this post is the best I can do.

I’m also sorry for the curtness of my interactions with you, and the cynical tone you might pick up from this post, but again it is a matter of necessity to avoid the burn-out that many others have suffered, and to ensure I can give a good account for how I’ve used my life ( Romans 14:12 ).

It might be that you have used an AI to generate something, or you’ve worked hard on it yourself, and you think it looks pretty good, but it is still labelled slop. Below are some clues as to why that might be. You will have to work through these yourself and see which apply to yours.

The best summary I can give for what I’m looking for in a good quality code contribution is the following:

Every single line, word, token and character should have been written with the understanding that another human being will need to read it, understand it and potentially maintain it indefinitely. This covers:

descriptions and comments in pull requests

Of course, the code must actually work (that’s step zero, the computer has to understand it too), and in addition, it must be for the benefit of all current and future users, which means it mustn’t recklessly break anything, for example, and must be designed with long term needs in mind.

In short, the contribution should treat the recipients (reviewers and maintainers) as human beings whose time is extremely valuable, and the project as something valuable that needs to be protected.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

마치 테러리스트가 인질극 벌이는데 인질 죽는다고 테러리스트 진압 안하겠다는 것과 같은 말이다.

총수, 의장 검찰 총원해서 조져 놓다가 사면을 해놓으니까 버릇이 안좋아 진건지 아니면 반도체좀 했다고 뭐가 된양인지 모르겠다만

앞으로 대한민국에서도 여당과 야당 합작으로 대기업 총수, 의장 사법처리하고 사면하지않고 만기 출소하는 케이스가 단 한 번이라도 나와서 명확하게 그 선례를 남겨놔야한다는게 내 생

Two months ago, I got a new laptop. It’s a Lenovo Thinkpad z61t. I actually ordered a t61, but I accidentally got the z61 instead — and, I actually really like it. items.title: Squircles
items.summary: graphics
items.content:
A squircle is a shape intermediate between a square and a circle.

There is no single mathematical definition, rather there are a number of curves that fit this shape.

All general squircles are parametrized, and can vary between circle and square.

The best known squircle is the superellipse, popularized by Piet Hein.

Martin Gardner wrote a detailed narrative of its origin in a Scientific American column in 1977.

The text is replicated in https://piethein.com/superellipse/ but that’s missing equations and figures.

The superellipse has the formula $|x|^n + |y|^n = 1$ (we’ll use a unit radius for convenience).

When $n=2$ it is a circle, and it approaches a square asymptotically as $n \rightarrow \infty$.

There is no standard measurement for squircles.

For superellipses, the exponent is the most common parameter.

A good choice is the coordinates of the midpoint of the quadrant, assuming a unit radius; here $x$ and $y$ are equal.

The conversion formula is simple and intuitive: $x = 0.5^{1/n}$.

This measurement is called "gauge" in the interactive demo above, and is the primary parameter; with the exception of some unreachable regions of parameter space, it should be possible to compare different squircle variants with similar gauge.

There are two basic approaches to squircle creation.

One is a single analytic curve, where curvature reaches zero at the poles, but is otherwise nonzero.

The other is mixing straight line segments with corners.

A significant advantage of the latter approach is that it can adapt to rectangles of arbitrary aspect ratio without distorting the corner shape.

Squircles received renewed attention when Apple changed the icon shape from rounded rectangle to their own squircle in iOS 7 in 2013.

There were several blog posts to analyze and recreate the shape.

An early analysis suggested that it was a superellipse of exponent 5, but when people extracted the Béziers and looked more closely, that was found to be inaccurate.

For the raw Bézier path data of the Apple shape, the best source is the PaintCode blog .

This blog correctly points out some bugs in that logic, and also has some details on behavior for oval rather than square aspect ratios.

The Apple shape has a number of flaws, including one extraneous straight line segment, and a lack of symmetry.

However, those flaws are minor, and really only reveal themselves under close analysis.

The Apple shape has no additional parameter, so its variation is controlled entirely by the length of the flat side.

With no flat side, it has a gauge fixed at 0.809.

An extremely detailed analysis of the Apple shape is in The Art of Continuous Corners .

Figma published a blog post, Desperately Seeking Squircles , with an analysis of the Apple squircle and their own approximation.

It is influential because Figma is an important design tool, because their writeup was compelling, and because there are any number of open source implementations of it, mostly TypeScript/JavaScript.

The Figma blog contains a plot of the Béziers comprising a cleaned up version of iOS 7 rounded rectangle, revealing three Bézier segments per quadrant.

It fixes the straight-line segment and the asymmetry, so is not an exact match.

The middle segment is very close to an arc.

The other segments are more problematic.

They have zero curvature at the endpoints, so are G2 continuous with flat sides, but there is a curvature discontinuity with the middle (arc) section, and their curvature profile is not especially smooth.

A reasonable guess is that it was drawn by hand to be approximately smooth.

Without a flat side, the Figma squircle is only capable of a gauge between $\sqrt{0.5}$ (0.707) and 0.854.

Gauges up to 1 are of course attainable by adding the flat side.

The Figma blog suggests “smoothed curvature profiles” which have a piecewise linear relationship between arc length and curvature.

Martin Gardner는 1977년 Scientific American 칼럼에서 그 기원을 자세히 소개했다. 초타원의 식은 |x|^n + |y|^n = 1이며, 단위 반지름을 기준으로 한다. n=2일 때 원이 되고, n이 무한대로 갈수록 정사각형에 가까워진다. 표준 측정 방식은 없지만 지수 n이 가장 흔한 매개변수다. 단위 반지름에서 사분원의 중점 좌표는 x = 0.5^(1/n)으로 계산되며, 이 값은 대화형 데모에서 'gauge'라고 불린다.

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: Revealed: Israel uploaded millions of photos to Amazon’s facial recognition platform to track Palestinians
items.content:
Revealed: Israel uploaded millions of photos to Amazon’s facial recognition platform to track Palestinians

Israel has in recent years migrated huge volumes of data into Amazon’s datacentres. Illustration: Guardian Design

Upload came as the Israeli military was increasing its reliance on Amazon’s cloud platform to meet the technological demands of its bombardment of Gaza

The Israeli military uploaded 3.5m photos to Amazon’s cloud platform in order to use the US company’s facial recognition technology to analyse images of Palestinians, the Guardian can reveal.

Leaked documents show the expansive catalogue of images was moved into Amazon’s cloud in the early months of Israel’s devastating aerial bombardment and ground offensive in Gaza.

The images were uploaded by a department of the Israeli military that holds a vast collection of photos covering the Palestinian populations in Gaza and the West Bank .

The department informed Amazon of the decision to upload the images in early 2024 so it could use Rekognition, the company’s AI-powered image analysis platform for a facial recognition project.

The documents obtained by the Guardian form part of an investigation into the Israeli military’s reliance on the technology and infrastructure of Amazon’s cloud computing business to monitor Palestinians.

According to the files and interviews with military sources, Israel has in recent years migrated huge volumes of data – including sensitive intelligence material and information about Palestinians living under occupation – into Amazon’s datacentres.

The large set of images was moved into an Amazon datacentre near Tel Aviv by a department commonly known as Rolling Stone, which sits within a military software unit.

Displaced Palestinians wait to cross a checkpoint in Mughraqa in central Gaza in January 2025. Photograph: Eyad Baba/AFP/Getty Images The department takes its name from a system widely used by the Israeli military that serves as a central repository of information about Palestinians living in Gaza and the West Bank.

At the time, the department was exploring using facial recognition technologies to analyse the extensive catalogues of images of Palestinians it holds, several sources with knowledge of its work said.

After Israel’s ground invasion of Gaza in October 2023, its military routinely collected images of Palestinians as they passed through checkpoints, often after they had been forcibly displaced by the bombing campaign.

It’s not clear whether the 3.5m images uploaded to Amazon’s Rekognition were captured at these checkpoints, which effectively served as pop-up surveillance posts.

However, a military source familiar with facial recognition efforts at the checkpoints said Amazon’s cloud infrastructure was used due to the “very large scale” of images collected at the sites.

Israel has long used facial recognition technology, particularly in its occupation of the West Bank. Face scanning is routine at checkpoints, while Israeli soldiers use custom-built smartphone apps to collect images of people living in the Palestinian territory.

In the early stages of its campaign in Gaza, Israel used Rekognition to identify hostages captured by militants in the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023. The military also deployed facial recognition technology to identify people it suspected were militants.

The New York Times has previously reported how the military experimented with commercially available technology in Gaza to detect faces in crowds and in drone footage, at times wrongly flagging civilians as militants.

The new documents reveal the Israeli military’s use of Amazon technology, both for experiments with facial recognition and for a more far-reaching project to move its data on to the servers of the computing arm of the conglomerate founded by billionaire Jeff Bezos .

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 집에서 한 말이나 제 언니랑 한 말들을 학교 가면 다 알고있어요 그래서 제가 말한 내용이랑 똑같은 내용을 꼭 제가 들을 수 있을때 언급하고 남자애들 여자애들 할것없이 제가 안보이는 데에서 조금만 이상한 말 하면 비웃으면서 지나가요 ㅠ 제가 진짜 친구가 없어서 학교에서 한마디도 안하는 날들이 대부분인데 제가 언니랑 학교 구석에서 말한 내용이랑 집에서 혼잣말 한 내용들을 똑같이 언급한게 한두번이 아니에요 ㅠ 제가 그냥 내용만 겹치면 말을 않겠는데 제가 말했던 내용 언급하면서 꼭 제 이름도 한번씩 부르고 그래요 보통 사람들은 자기이름을 그렇게 말하면 기분나빠서 한번 돌아보기라도 하겠지만 저는 성격이 워낙 내성적이라 누가 비웃고 지나가거나 째려보거나 저 보면서 한숨쉬어도 아무말도 못하거든요 ㅠ 그래서 그냥 기분만 나쁜건데 이게 하루이틀 쌓이니까 너무 힘들더라고요 ㅠ 처음엔 저도 이게 정신이 약간 아픈건가 했는데 정신병 관련 영상도 다 보고 그랬는데 환청은 이런식으로 들리는게 아니라고 하더라고요 계속 날 비난하고 그런식으로 들리는건데 저는 그런게 전혀 아니라 제가 전날 했던 얘기들, 방금 쉬는시간에 학교 구석에서 나눈 얘기들을 자꾸 똑같이 언급하니까 미치겠어요 ㅠ 한두번 우연으로 겹치는게 아니라 계속 겹쳐요 진짜.. 그리고 애초에 제가 학교에서 말을 한마디도 안하는데 자꾸 저한테 그런 반응을 보인다는게 애초에 저한테 이상한 일이 일어난다는 반증 아닌가요? 그리고 걔네가 말했던걸 몇개를 말씀드려보면 제가 도청을 의심한 초기에 급식실에서 밥먹고있었는데 어떤 남자애가 “도청” 이러고 지나가는거에요 그리고 저희반 남자애가 제 언니 이동수업반이랑 같은 반인데 거기서 쉬는시간에 “도청기를 달고다녀 ㅋㅋㅋㅋ” 이랬다는거에요 진짜 이상하죠 저는 예전에 우울증 약을 먹은적이 있어서 정신이 막 무결점으로 건강한 편은 아니에요 근데 저희 언니는 그런적도 없고 교우관계도 좋고 진짜 정신이 건강하거든요 ㅠ 근데 저희 언니가 그런말을 들었다니깐 진짜 도청이 일어나는게 맞는거구나 생각했어요.. 그리고 또 있었던 일을 말씀드리면 이동수업 때 제 뒷쪽에서 남자애가 제 아버지 직업을 언급하면서 제 이름을 말하는거에요 이게 도청을 하지 않고서는 절대 알수가 없는 사실이거든요 ㅠ 또 “정신병ㅋㅋㅋ” 하면서 제 이름을 언급하는거에요 이것도 도청을 하지 않았다면 알수 없는거고요 더 말씀드릴 사례가 많은데 그러면 너무 길어져서 이정도만 말씀드릴게요 그래서 찾아보니까 머리에 붙일수 있는 초소형 도청기가 있다길래  제 언니가 제 머리를 샅샅이 뒤져줬거든요? 근데 그래도 아무것도 안나오더라고요 ㅠ 그리고 또 도청 탐지 업체를 알아보니까 금액이 너무 비싸서요 ㅠ 제가 고3인데 이런일을 당해서 너무 스트레스 받는데 방법이 없어서 정말 어떻게 해야될지 모르겠어요 안그래도 제가 여자애들이나 남자애들이 괴롭힐 소재가 많은 조용한 애거든요 ㅠ그래서 저를 지나칠때 꼭 한마디 끼얹고 지나가고 그래서 학교생활이 막 편한 그런애는 아닌데 학교에서 유일하게 맘놓고 말할 수 있는 언니랑 말하는 얘기를 다 알고있으니까 스트레스 받아서 공부 능력도 점점 떨어지는것같고 쨋든 걱정이 이만저만이 아니에요 어떡해야되죠 ㅠㅠ 제가 성격이 활발한 편도 아니고 집에 돈이 많지도 않아서 진짜 대학 잘가야되는데 걱정이에요ㅠㅠ 긴글 읽어주셔서 감사하고요 여기가 사생활 침해 관련한 갤러리니까 혹여나 저랑 비슷한 경험이 있으시거나 관련 지식이 있는 분은 제가 어떻게 해야하는건지 알려주시면 진짜진짜 감사드릴것같아요 많은 도움 부탁드려요 정말 방법 여러가지 찾아봐도 안되겠어서 여기다 글 남겨요

items.title: Janet Reno was talking about my friend Coolio (computer criminal)
items.summary: culture, security
items.content:
AI disclosure: this story was written entirely by human hands, with AI doing proof-reading and light edits.

No, not the rapper Coolio, but rather Dennis M. Moran .

There I was, standing on the couch in my basement, pointing at the TV. Janet Reno is giving a press conference on CNN, vowing to bring these cyber terrorists to justice. My jaw is open, I’m laughing. I can’t believe it. She’s talking about my friend Dennis “Coolio” Moran, a 17-year-old.

We were the #goonies on EFNet. We broke off from #doom, following our friend chunkk, the legendary Doom player (I still haven’t seen The Goonies movie though). Some of these people are still very close friends and at the time they were much closer friends than anyone I had IRL since they were computer elite and my local friends were all llamas. Above all, we were still very teenage and very dumb.

They were fond of robotripping, since it was all the drugs teenagers could afford. As a suburban kid from Queens from a loving supportive family I knew drugs were bad and would sit this stuff out. I had a job at a dialup ISP in Manhattan called nyct.net as a FreeBSD sys admin. I was moving up in the world.

Others, not so much. The most extreme robotripper and psychonaut on #goonies was Coolio. He was also a lot of fun. He basically never spoke ill of anyone. Everyone loved him. Girls would fall for him just watching him say stuff on IRC over my shoulder.

He was also the poorest friend I’ve ever had. He grew up in Wolfeboro, New Hampshire. His mom wasn’t in his life and his dad was, as far as I knew, a decent fellow, though they struggled to make ends meet and he had lived out of a tent for a period of his life. People mostly sort their friends and they get a picture of the world that’s very curated. Dennis (and indeed the rest of IRC) was my window out of my Queens NY bubble.

We did eventually hang out IRL. Dennis came to visit me in NYC and we went to Mindless Self Indulgence shows together, which were insanely fun. After one of them the (freakishly tall) lead singer Little Jimmy Urine was offering kisses for $5 (“VD free”). Dennis offered $20 over the heads of a bunch of clawing girls and he and Jimmy Urine made out.

When he wasn’t talking about drugs or girls, he was talking about hacking. We were all dabbling in computer stuff. We loved Doom and Quake and we had aspirations about becoming game developers. I bought a book on C and installed DJGPP and was trying my best to learn, but lost interest in games and pivoted to networks and coding on Linux. And also hacking. Though it had been out for years, I had just caught up with that Phrack article about Smashing the Stack for Fun and Profit and was curious about how to apply it. Dennis was interested too, and we thought about how cool it’d be to write a PoC exploit together.

Dennis found out about a BIND vulnerability with no PoC. We wrote one together. It worked! We were pumped. I thought we should promote internet health by publishing the PoC, since that was how you got people to fix bugs in those days. Dennis goes quiet for a few days. Then he comes back. Bro had been busy, he hacked into all of the vulnerable servers and recruited them into an insane botnet. I was shocked. WTF was he going to do with this? I thought we were just learning and there he goes hacking into half of the DNS servers on the internet! At least he patched BIND for them afterwards.

Dennis reads about the CD Universe extortion attempt and sees a business idea. What if he combines his botnet with smurfing to do massive DDoS attacks? Then he could threaten to knock sites offline if they didn’t pay. I thought this sounded crazy but he insisted on trying. His reasoning was you can’t just cold email executives out of nowhere and try to extort them. You gotta build up a reputation first. So he flexed his muscle and took down Yahoo!

He would say “watch this” and the sites would go down. First Yahoo, then buy.com and eBay, then etrade.com.

He picked buy.com…

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. Trump administration moves to block China from indirect access to American AI tech

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Monday issued new rules to restrict remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers, marking the latest step to limit China's abilities to use U.S. chips to train their best artificial intelligence models.

The rule also was issued days after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO amid scrutiny of his ties to a Chinese executive who used to lead Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which is suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls. The company provides computing power to Chinese companies using chips housed in Southeast Asian data centers, including facilities in Malaysia.

"The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the Bureau of Industry and Security under the Commerce Department said in issuing the rule that took effect immediately.

READ MORE: Could everything be broken? Grounded jets, Microsoft outage, AI chaos make some wonder

Under the new rule, overseas data centers that serve companies in countries including China, Russia, Iran and Cuba are required to identify their end users. There also will be an additional, case-by-case licensing requirements for sales of chips for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil — countries that "present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion" to unauthorized destinations, the rule says.

The U.S. bans sales of the country's most advanced AI chips to China, seeking to maintain an edge in its rivalry with China for predominance in artificial intelligence. However, many lawmakers and policymakers believe the country's export control rules are not tough enough and filled with loopholes such as cloud computing that allow China to rent processing power built on American technology.

Last year, U.S. Rep. Michael Lawler, a New York Republican, introduced a bill to broaden the U.S. export controls to include remote access. He told Congress "physical export controls" under current rules do not apply to remote access, allowing China to "access our tech through the cloud" and giving it "a real tool to sidestep" U.S. export restrictions. The bill has passed the House.

items.title: 33% of gamedevs laid off over 2 years: GDC 2026 State of the Game Industry
items.content:
This past year, the Game Developers Conference transformed, becoming the GDC Festival of Gaming . The State of the Game Industry has also transformed, expanding to better represent the full game ecosystem. Organizers of the GDC Festival of Gaming have released the 2026 State of the Game Industry report, offering insights into key game industry trends based on responses from more than 2,300 game industry professionals.

To represent the thoughts and perspectives of the game industry across roles and disciplines, we consulted key stakeholders and community members to refine questions and broaden the survey’s reach. Surveys were customized for each participant group, ensuring that developers, marketers, executives, investors, and others answered questions most relevant to them. We also surveyed a smaller group of game educators and students to capture a snapshot of the challenges facing the next generation.

The report provides the latest data and analysis on layoffs, generative AI adoption and sentiment, US unionization efforts, development platforms and priorities, business pressures, emerging trends, and more.

Here are some highlights from the 2026 State of the Game Industry .

The effects of recent layoffs continue to spread across the industry. Over one in four (28%) survey respondents were laid off in the past two years, increasing to one-third (33%) for those in the United States, and half said their current (or most recent) employer has conducted layoffs in the past 12 months. Those at AAA studios were highly likely to have experienced layoffs at their companies; two-thirds of respondents at AAA studios said their companies had layoffs. One-third of people working at indie studios reported the same.

The smaller survey of students illustrates widespread pessimism among future developers and leaders eager to enter the space. Three-fourths (74%) of surveyed students said they are concerned about their future job prospects in the game industry. Students noted the lack of entry-level jobs, increased competition from laid-off workers with more experience and AI-led displacement.

Newly added to the 2026 survey, Valve’s Steam Deck is the fourth-most-developed-for platform among respondents, with 28% of developers making or optimizing games for the PC handheld. In addition, 40% of developers said they’re interested in making games for Steam Deck, putting it on par with the Nintendo Switch 2 (39%). For future game development, PC continues to reign, with 73% of survey executives placing PC in their top 3 next-gen platform they’re most interested in.

Unreal Engine is the most popular engine among survey respondents. 42% of developers reported that it is their primary engine for game development, ahead of the next-most-popular engine, Unity, at 30%. Unreal Engine adoption appears to be more common for developers at AA (59%) and AAA (47%) studios. A majority (54%) of developers at older indie studios are still using Unity. Godot has gained some use with newer indie developers (11%), but less so with those at more established studios.

Survey results indicate that over one-third (36%) of game industry professionals are using generative AI tools as part of their job. 30% of respondents at game studios reported using AI tools, which is far less than the 58% of those at publishing companies, support teams, and marketing/PR firms that reported to use AI tools. Business professionals’ use (58%) far outweighs that of most other disciplines.

Sentiment from game Industry professionals reveal that they often balance the use of multiple AI tools for multiple purposes, rather than relying on a single platform or use. The most used AI tool for game industry professionals are large language models (LLMs)—mainly ChatGPT (74%), followed by Google Gemini (37%) and Microsoft Copilot (22%). The most common use is research or brainstorming (81%), followed by daily tasks (like writing emails) and code assistance (47% each), and prototyping…

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

our 3rd release, a full color 31.5" ePaper display in a handmade wooden frame, is now available for pre-order. watch the short film:

the 1st batch is just ~470 units and i intend to ship at least a few by the end of 2026. most deliveries will happen early 2027. see logistics for more details or pre-order here .

in 2013 i founded ArtSpot. our vision was to give New Yorkers a bit of joy by exposing them to local art. we did this through informal agreements with dozens of cafes, small galleries, and restaurants. " let us curate art on your walls, get paid if someone buys it. "

and it worked. sort of. finding artists was easy, building the platform was easy. getting permission from venues was slow but straightforward. the problem was nobody actually bought the art. i remember the admin email notification that first time a piece was sold. it was a small painting of Janelle Monáe. the buyer was my friend, a gift to me. here it is, still in my possession.

anyway ArtSpot failed. five years later i paid back my investors (+ 13% interest). but the vision never went away. i love making and consuming art.

i probably say " the most popular feature request since launch is ______ " too often. after saying no (and yes) to so many requests, it's tough to keep count.

but with certainty, one of our strongest convictions was about color. TRMNL is not a television. it is not a clock. we avoid trying to do too much.

then grayscale happened . photos look great. art is possible. community member Clark debuted Jaws (yes the movie), 1 frame at a time .

which got us thinking... maybe we were wrong about color. maybe it aligns with our vision and just maybe, it makes it even bigger.

today i'm thrilled to bury the lede and announce Frame . it's a 31.5 inch full color ePaper display, enclosed in a hand made wooden body that we manufacture ourselves. yes, we opened our own woodworking shop a few miles from HQ. a closer look at the workshop is coming soon.

Frame gets all the same features as other TRMNL devices, with a few additional perks spanning both the web platform and the hardware itself. watch the short film or read along below.

often requested, always ignored, until now. Frame will update at specified moments of the day versus a relative "every N minutes" cadence. this reduces screen flicker while also extending the battery life and adding continuity to your schedule.

the internet is cool but totally unnecessary. Frame's microSD port lets you run devices completely offline with zero personal information reaching our servers.

like all TRMNL devices, a rechargeable battery is included (10-20k mAh available). but with Frame we added an extra USB-C port on the rear of the device, accessible with a small hole through the back panel for always-on connectivity.

some of my colleagues are snobs about ePaper dithering algorithms and LUTs (look-up tables). this is now your gain.

over the past few months we've been developing Lazarus, a color conversion engine that we think provides Frame the best color matching on the market for any Spectra 6 display. it's also coming soon to our 4-color device , and yes it will be open source for your own tuning pleasure.

Frame at Cafe Brûlée in LaGrange, Georgia

we're negotiating with some of our favorite community developers to build more Frame-centric features. paying homage to ArtSpot , we just created a Local Art plugin where anyone can submit their work and even sell it through the TRMNL platform.

items.title: How Rust Changed Me As A Developer
items.summary: performance, rust
items.content:
The programming language you use affects how you think as a software developer

1 . That may seem surprising to you; you may have picked up JavaScript

pretty quickly knowing Python, and it didn't really affect how you think or

develop. That's because those languages are pretty similar. The more different a

programming language is from what you're used to, the more it can change you.

Rust was quite different to me, so it did.

I've been developing with Rust for over 6 years; more than 4 years

now . One of the reasons I really wanted to

become more proficient with Rust is because I knew it would challenge me, and

hopefully change me for the better as a developer. I think it did.

What I learned and am going to discuss here is not exclusive to Rust. You can

encounter many of these concepts in other contexts, and indeed I had encountered

quite a few of them already. But in this case, Rust helped bring them into

We're all familiar with product types, though not usually under that name:

The fields of the Human struct 2 can vary independently from each

other, and we have to deal with all possible combinations: all possible first

names and last names, combined. The product of their combinations, to to

But it turns out there's another type thing that's been around forever but that

the programming community has mostly been been ignoring 3 : the sum

type. A sum type expresses variants: something is either one thing, or another,

Human { first_name: String , last_name: String },

Cat { name: String , cuteness: Cuteness }

A Person is either a human or a cat: that's the sum of the possiblities.

Each variant can have data associated with it, and this can be a product type,

but the Person type is just these options (two in this case). In code where

you need to deal with a person, you need to handle each variant by match in on

the object. The Rust compiler enforces this.

// do a thing with first_name and last_name

When you handle the human variant, you only need to worry about first_name and

last_name . You don't have to worry about name or cuteness at all. These

It turns out that it's really helpful to model stuff using sum types. People

using functional programming languages already knew this. You can model

optionality ( null ) this way: you got either some value, or nothing. You can

also model errors: it's either okay (with whatever value you return in case of

success), or an error (with a value describing the error).

Any language without sum types now feels impoverished to me. I know I can

simulate it with some type field, but the job of a programming language is to

help me handle basic stuff, and this is basic stuff.

In an object oriented programming language, you handle variants using dynamic

dispatch and an interface (or inheritance). You do this:

The idea is that you can now use Person anywhere without worrying about the

details inside: it's loosely coupled. You only use their interface.

This is indeed a great idea, but Rust taught me that this has tradeoffs I may

not want to pay for. You pay two things: performance, and the need to create the

Let's talk about the need to create the interface. You need to devise an

interface that actually makes sense for your application: how are you using

humans and cats everywhere? Doing this work of abstraction may be extremely

worthwhile to do, especially if you anticipate unknown future persons that you

need to be able to plug in later without having to modify the code that uses

them -- you want your code use the open/closed

But what if you are developing a single domain, and inside that you just want to

be able to handle cats and humans and that's it? There's just no need to plug in

other types of persons, and certainly not from outside.

Or let's say you do want to add a new variant once every while. Say you want to

add Dog . Maybe you're actually okay going through the code that handles

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…
